page: Amazon Web Services c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 4.5 GHz, with one thread per core. Memory configuration includes 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying on external network storage solutions, and provides a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across single-core and multi-core CPU metrics. In Geekbench, the instance achieves a single-core score of 2631.0 and a multi-core score of 24632.0, both placing in the top 10%. Stress-ng tests reinforce this compute density with 3773.56 in single-core and 120278.88 in multi-core throughput. Data handling and compression show top-tier performance, reaching 41.47 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.44 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, supplemented by a strong PassMark database operations result of 41207.15.

Hardware vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 support lightweight machine learning workloads. For small 135M language models, the instance achieves top-tier throughput of 5443.98 tokens/sec during prompt processing and 408.76 tokens/sec during text generation. For medium 7B models, text generation remains top-tier at 43.62 tokens/sec, while prompt processing reaches 216.76 tokens/sec. Cache hierarchy consists of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache.

By omitting local NVMe drives and GPUs, the c8a.8xlarge delivers targeted cost efficiency for raw CPU computation without the overhead of unneeded accelerator hardware. Tradeoffs include reliance on attached storage over EBS, as well as memory density capped at 2.0 GB per core. The server is well suited for compute-intensive workloads, including continuous integration build pipelines, batch compression, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AMD EPYC 9R45 x86_64 processor on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread allocation, backed by 64.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and 15 Gbps baseline networking. The hardware contains no onboard GPUs or local storage. CPU benchmark performance ranks in the top decile, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 24632.0 and single-core score of 2631.0, paired with top-tier compression and database operation results. AVX-512 vector extensions support efficient small-to-medium LLM CPU inference. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-heavy workloads, making it well matched for software compilation, batch processing, data compression, and CPU-bound web serving that do not require local ephemeral disks.
